paragraphs: The X5 xDrive50e has been a mainstay of the X5 diesel range since 2012, spanning two generations under one badge. Early G05 models from 2012 to 2015 use the N47, a 2.0-litre diesel that's part of a family known for a specific timing chain issue. From late 2015 onwards, across both the G05 and later the G05, the X5 xDrive50e switched to the B47, a newer, significantly more reliable unit that doesn't share the N47's timing chain concerns. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and the known wear pattern differ - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The X5 xDrive50e is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: The B58 is a 3.0-litre inline-six petrol engine, fitted to the current-generation X5 xDrive50e as the internal combustion component of its plug-in hybrid powertrain. No widely-reported engine issue has been confirmed for this specific variant.

compatibility.intro: The X5 xDrive50e's powertrain is specific to the G05 generation, combining the B58 engine with a high-voltage electric motor and battery pack. Compatibility depends not only on the engine code but on the specific hybrid system configuration. We always confirm your exact build via registration or VIN before quoting any work, ensuring every component matches your vehicle's original specification.
